restrictions: van Oorschot--Wiener parallel collision search with distinguished points on the single-block iteration f(s) = SHA-256-r31(embed(s)), where embed injectively writes a 256-bit state into 32 of 55 content bytes (remaining 23 bytes a fixed public constant), so each f-evaluation is exactly one target compression and any image collision yields two distinct valid 55-byte messages with equal complete 256-bit digests.

Distinguishing predicate: low 88 bits zero, theta = 2^-88; trails capped at L_max = 20/theta; a repeated distinguished endpoint is resolved by lockstep re-walk to the exact colliding predecessor pair, which is then verified by complete re-hashing and message-inequality check.
Evaluation budget B = 2^128.5; report FAIL if exhausted. Correctness is unconditional; only the expected-running-time bound relies on the declared random-mapping heuristic H1.

preprocessing is inside total time; nonuniform_advice_log2_bytes = 0 reflects zero actual advice, no precomputed collision and no favorable seed; memory_log2_bytes = 48 covers at most 2^40.5 stored distinguished points plus fixed scratch.

time_log2 = 129 is a declared upper bound on the charged total (B compressions plus O(B/C) wrapper operations plus negligible collision-location cost). This uses no property of the round reduction and claims no improvement over the nominal reference.

heuristics.statement: For the purpose of bounding the expected number of f-evaluations to the first image collision, the fixed single-block iteration f(s) = SHA-256-r31(embed(s)) behaves as a uniform random mapping on its 2^256-point state space, so the expected work to a collision is sqrt(pi*N/2) = sqrt(pi/2)*2^128 < 2^128.33 evaluations and Pr(collision within B = 2^128.5 evaluations) ~ 1 - exp(-B^2/(2N)) > 0.63.
heuristics.scope: Applies only to the average-case expected-time and success-probability analysis of the distinguished-point search. It is not used for correctness: any returned pair is a verified collision independent of H1, and the algorithm reports FAIL rather than a false collision if the budget is exhausted.
heuristics.extrapolation: The random-mapping model is applied at the full 2^256 state space and the full evaluation budget B = 2^128.5; no finite experiment is extrapolated, and no per-round or structural property of the 31-round reduction is assumed. The bound is the standard birthday/rho scaling evaluated at these sizes.
heuristics.limitations: H1 is an average-case premise about one specific fixed function, not a worst-case theorem; a pathological f with anomalously long tails, short cycles, or many fixed points could inflate the expected time. It is unproven for SHA-256-r31, which is precisely why this is an exploratory rather than a rigorous claim and why a companion unconditional birthday construction at the same time (with much larger memory) exists.
